research_mode: official Home Office, ONS and OSR sources only; outcome 14-22 definitions, CSEW response/reporting and weighting, police-recorded revision/QA, comparability and governance controls; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Outcome 14 definition
verified_claims: Outcome 14 applies where no named suspect has been identified
the crime is confirmed
the victim declines or is unable to support further police action to identify the offender
limitations: it must not be merged with outcome 16, where a suspect is identified
victim non-support is not proof that the offence did not occur

sources.name: Outcome 15 definition
verified_claims: Outcome 15 applies where a named suspect has been identified
the victim supports police action
evidential difficulties prevent further action and can include a wanted suspect who cannot be traced
limitations: it must not be merged with victim-withdrawal outcomes
a wanted-but-untraced case is not a conviction or completed prosecution

sources.name: Outcome 16 definition
verified_claims: Outcome 16 applies where a named suspect has been identified
the victim does not support or withdraws support from police action
the category is victim-based evidential difficulty
limitations: withdrawal must not be treated as evidence that the crime was false
it must remain separate from outcome 14 and outcome 15

sources.name: Outcome 17 definition
verified_claims: Outcome 17 applies where a suspect has been identified
the prosecution time limit has expired
the category was introduced from April 2014
limitations: it applies only to offences with a prosecution time limit
expiry is a procedural outcome rather than a harm or safety measure

sources.name: Outcome 18 definition
verified_claims: Outcome 18 applies where no suspect has been identified
the crime has been investigated as far as reasonably possible
the case is closed pending further investigative opportunities
limitations: closure does not mean the offence did not occur
future investigative opportunities can reopen activity

sources.name: Outcome 19 definition
verified_claims: Outcome 19 is an NFIB-only fraud outcome
a fraud crime has been recorded
the NFIB assessment found insufficient lines of enquiry to allocate it for investigation
limitations: it must not be applied to non-NFIB offences
filing is not proof that the report was invalid

sources.name: Outcome 20 definition
verified_claims: Outcome 20 applies where another body or agency will undertake further action
the victim or representative must be made aware of the action
the outcome was introduced from April 2015
limitations: the responsible external body is not automatically identified in aggregate statistics
the outcome is not equivalent to police inaction

sources.name: Outcome 21 definition
verified_claims: Outcome 21 applies where a suspect is identified
further investigation could provide evidence sufficient for formal action
the police decide that further action is not in the public interest
limitations: it must not be merged with outcome 10 or CPS outcome 9 without definition checks
public-interest decisions are not severity rankings

sources.name: Outcome 22 definition
verified_claims: Outcome 22 requires diversionary, educational or intervention activity
after that activity it is not in the public interest to take further action
collection was voluntary from April 2019
limitations: voluntary introduction affects early coverage
activity completion is not a conviction or universal success measure

sources.name: Outcomes 14 to 22 introduction matrix
verified_claims: outcomes 14 to 19 date from April 2014
outcome 20 dates from April 2015 and outcome 21 from January 2016
outcome 22 was voluntary from April 2019
limitations: time-series comparisons require outcome-specific start dates
availability must not be backfilled into earlier periods
